title: Week Ahead: US Midterms, Apple Earnings and October Jobs
summary: US midterms, earnings from Apple, Palantir and AMD, and October payrolls headline Wall Street's week. Here is the calendar and the market mood.
body_markdown:
Both dissenters, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, wanted a quarter-point hike. The Fed's statement also said inflation remains elevated.


A payrolls number well above forecasts could strengthen the case for a hike at the December 9 meeting. A weak number could ease that pressure.


On the midterms, CNBC notes that early polling and prediction markets give Democrats a shot at both chambers of Congress. So far, investors expect limited direct market impact.


Still, a change in Congress could shift policy in a few areas:


- Possible cuts to defense spending.
- More pricing pressure on drugmakers.
- New regulation for data centers.


## This Week's Earnings Calendar


According to FactSet, as of October 30, 60% of S&P 500 companies had reported Q3 2026 results. The index's blended earnings growth rate stood at 30.2% year over year, and 82% of companies had beaten EPS estimates.


That 30.2% is up from an estimate of 29.1% on September 30, and FactSet adds that 70% of companies have beaten revenue estimates.


The beats are smaller than usual, though. According to CNBC, companies are topping EPS estimates by 1.4% on average, well below the five-year average of 7.5% in FactSet data.


For the fourth quarter, FactSet counts 28 S&P 500 companies with positive EPS guidance and 19 with negative guidance. The index trades at 18.7 times forward earnings, below its five-year average of 19.8.


Here is when some of the week's larger companies report, with consensus EPS estimates from Nasdaq:


- **[Apple (AAPL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/aapl/) , Monday, Nov. 2, after the close:** consensus EPS of $1.98. The market will read gross margins and the effect of the latest iPhone launch timing.
- **[Palantir (PLTR)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/pltr/) , Monday, Nov. 2, after the close:** consensus EPS of $0.33. The market will read revenue growth from US government and commercial clients.
- **[Airbnb (ABNB)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/abnb/) , Thursday, Nov. 5, after the close:** consensus EPS of $2.89. The market will read travel booking trends and the fourth-quarter outlook.


Other reports scheduled this week:


- **[AMD (AMD)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amd/) , Tuesday, Nov. 3, after the close:** the focus is on AI chip demand from data centers.
- **[Uber (UBER)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/uber/) , Wednesday, Nov. 4, before the open:** the focus is on gross bookings and trip volumes.
- **[McDonald's (MCD)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/mcd/) , Wednesday, Nov. 4, before the open:** the focus is on same-store sales and US consumer spending.
- **[Qualcomm (QCOM)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/qcom/) , Wednesday, Nov. 4, after the close:** the focus is on smartphone chip demand and its non-handset businesses.


If you trade from Asia, note that after-the-close releases land on the following morning in your time zone. The first full session to price in Apple and Palantir results is Tuesday in New York.


## Market Sentiment


Markets enter the week in a cautious mood. According to CNBC, the S&P 500 posted a losing week after disappointing results from[Amazon (AMZN)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amzn/) and[Intel (INTC)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/intc/) .


[Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/googl/) fell 12% on Thursday, its worst one-day drop on record, according to CNBC. That puts the largest tech names firmly in focus this week.


The central question is AI spending. CNBC reports that Amazon became the third hyperscaler, after Alphabet and[Meta (META)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/meta/) , to report negative free cash flow.


Investors are now asking less about how much is being spent on AI and more about when that spending turns into Profit. This week's chip reports will offer part of the answer.


Under the surface, most of the 11 S&P 500 sectors still gained last week, led by health care and consumer staples. That points to money rotating into defensive sectors rather than leaving the market altogether.


Historically, CNBC notes that November has been the Nasdaq's strongest month in midterm years, with an average gain of 3.5%. Past patterns do not guarantee the same outcome, especially with a rate hike still on the table.


Three things are likely to set the market's direction this week:


- The midterm results and how policy-sensitive sectors such as defense and pharma react.
- What companies say about AI spending and demand in their earnings calls.
- Friday's payrolls number and what it does to expectations for a December rate hike.


With elections, earnings and payrolls stacked into five sessions, Volatility could rise through the week. Keep the release schedule in view and understand the risks before you act.


This article is for education and information only and is not investment advice. Investment decisions are yours to make after your own research.
